description: Composite figure combining one high-resolution TEM lattice image (left, with a "5 nm" scale bar at lower right) and two selected-area electron diffraction (SAED) patterns inset at the right; the panels carry no (a)/(b) letters. In the HRTEM image two dashed boxes are drawn: a red box labelled "γ + Cu" at centre and a yellow box labelled "γ + κ" at top right, with fine lattice fringes running through both. Dashed connector lines link the yellow "γ + κ" box to the upper-right SAED pattern and the red "γ + Cu" box to the lower-right SAED pattern. The upper-right pattern is indexed with (011) and (111) reflections, labelled zone axis Z=[01̄1], with a 2 1/nm scale bar. The lower-right pattern is indexed with (1̄1̄1), (111) and (200) reflections, also Z=[01̄1], with a 2 1/nm scale bar. The caption states these are SAED patterns of the Cu-rich phase and κ-carbide in aged 3Cu steel. Taken together, the figure argues that austenite, κ-carbide and the Cu-rich phase are imaged along a common [011] axis, i.e. a cube-on-cube (111)γ//(111)κ//(111)Cu relationship; the citing text additionally assigns a BCC structure to the Cu-rich phase, which the labelled (111)-type reflections do not straightforwardly confirm.

observations.observation: The main panel is a high-resolution TEM lattice-fringe image with a printed scale bar of 5 nm at its lower right.
Two dashed boxes are drawn on the HRTEM image: a red box labelled "γ + Cu" in the centre and a yellow box labelled "γ + κ" at top right.
Dashed connector lines link the yellow "γ + κ" box to the upper-right SAED inset and the red "γ + Cu" box to the lower-right SAED inset.
The upper-right SAED inset is indexed with (011) and (111) reflections and labelled with zone axis Z=[01̄1] and a 2 1/nm scale bar.
The lower-right SAED inset is indexed with (1̄1̄1), (111) and (200) reflections and labelled with zone axis Z=[01̄1] and a 2 1/nm scale bar.

The caption states that Fig. 1 presents SAED patterns of the Cu-rich phase and κ-carbide in aged 3Cu steel, implying the two insets are the diffraction patterns of those two precipitates in the austenitic matrix.
The citing text states that according to SAED analysis the Cu-rich phase has BCC structure (Fig. 1, inset).
The citing text states that no additional diffraction spots are observed besides those of the Cu-rich phase and κ-carbide, indicating that both precipitates are coherent with the austenitic matrix.
The citing text infers from Fig. 1 a cube-on-cube orientation relationship [110]γ//[110]κ//[110]Cu and (111)γ//(111)κ//(111)Cu between austenite, κ-carbide and the Cu-rich phase.
The citing text reports interfacial energies of 0.025 J/m² for κ-carbide/austenite and 0.086 J/m² for Cu-rich phase/austenite, both lower than 0.1 J/m².

The lower-right (γ + Cu) pattern is labelled with (111)- and (1̄1̄1)-type reflections, which are normally forbidden for a BCC lattice; the image is therefore not fully reconciled with the citing text's assignment of a BCC structure to the Cu-rich phase.
Both SAED insets are labelled with the same zone axis, Z=[01̄1], consistent with the paper's argument that γ, κ-carbide and Cu-rich phase are viewed along a common direction.

subfigures.description: High-resolution TEM lattice-fringe image with a "5 nm" scale bar at lower right; two dashed boxes are marked, a red one labelled "γ + Cu" at centre and a yellow one labelled "γ + κ" at top right. Dashed lines lead from these boxes to the two SAED insets.
SAED pattern from the region marked "γ + κ"; index labels (011) and (111) with a zone-axis label Z=[01̄1] and a 2 1/nm scale bar.

unreadable_items: Weak/faint reflections in both SAED insets cannot be resolved at the supplied resolution; the exact crystallographic indices of the unlabelled spots are not verifiable
Whether the top-right inset belongs to the yellow 'γ + κ' region and the bottom-right inset to the red 'γ + Cu' region rests on the dashed connector lines, which are faint
The caption writes 'in-aged 3Cu steel'; the intended condition spelling (e.g. 'as-aged') is not confirmable from the image
